Chatsworth Courthouse

Address: 9425 Penfield Ave, Chatsworth, CA 91311

Phone: 818-407-2200

Chatsworth Courthouse case search for records can be found online using the Los Angeles court online portal https://www.lacourt.org/casesummary/ui/. The court maintains all the records online, in files, or in a database. You had to select the chatsworth courthouse and enter the case number. If you do not know the case number you cannot use this free online service for case searching. After entering the data, the case information will come. The portal will only show those records information that is publicly available.

The sealed records are not available for the viewing of the public. Some records are unavailable; if the information does not come, the case records will be removed or confidential and cannot be displayed online. You have to go to the court or give a record request for these documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information. The fee for each document per page is $0.50, which is mandatory when you come to the court for a records copy. If you want to search cases by name then you had to make an account or continue as a guest at https://www.lacourt.org/paonlineservices/pacommerce/login.aspx?appId=CDX&casetype=CIV. You had to pay a $4.75 fee per name search for these types of services.

Located in the scenic San Fernando Valley, the Chatsworth Courthouse serves as a hub for legal proceedings in Los Angeles County. As part of the County Superior Court system, the Chatsworth Courthouse handles a wide range of cases, including small claims, criminal, family law, and traffic matters. The Clerk's Office, situated within the chatsworth courthouse building, is available to assist visitors during regular business hours from Monday through Friday. When it comes to parking, a dedicated lot is conveniently located on the side of the chatsworth courthouse, ensuring easy access for all. The courthouse itself is known for its efficient operations and responsive staff, providing a welcoming and professional environment for legal matters.

Whether you need guidance on legal issues, are seeking the expertise of a lawyer, or simply want to learn more about the jurisdiction and judges presiding over your case, the chatsworth courthouse website is a valuable resource. Visitors and clients who have utilized the services of the Chatsworth Courthouse have expressed their satisfaction with the outcome of their cases and have been happy to recommend it to others in need of legal assistance. If you find yourself facing legal challenges, don't hesitate to reach out to the Chatsworth Courthouse. Their knowledgeable and friendly staff are ready to help navigate through your legal matters and ensure that you receive the support you need.

How do you make payments for tickets?

Chatsworth Courthouse pay ticket for traffic matters can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay in chatsworth courthouse for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the court payment window. Take your ticket and citation number with you when you come for payment. 2% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

Online payments can be made using the LA court Online Payment https://ww2.lacourt.org/trafficDL/ui/trafficOS.aspx?s=2&language=1. Retrieve your ticket information by finding your ticket using a case or traffic ticket number. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the online ticket payment option and pay the amount online. You will receive a confirmation message after your transaction is completed. All fines are not paid online, some cases require a personal appearance and you have to pay at the court. Service charges will be applied in this case. The Chatsworth Courthouse handles cases within the jurisdiction of the County Superior Court.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address; Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Phone

Tickets payment can also be made by calling 213 742-1884. Follow the instruction they tell you. Service charges will be applied in this case.

How can I take remote hearing?

Chatsworth Courthouse remote hearing is a permanent part of the LA court. You can schedule a free remote appearance in some cases by making an account at https://my.lacourt.org/laccwelcome. After the account is made, fill in the information related to the case and the court will respond with a schedule if your case is eligible for the online hearing except court holidays. The Clerk's Office is an essential part of the County Superior Court system, responsible for maintaining records and providing assistance to individuals involved in legal proceedings.

The Chatsworth Courthouse is the ideal place to handle a variety of legal issues, as it is known for its kind and open approach in helping individuals navigate through their cases. The experienced judges and staff have helped countless visitors during their time at the courthouse, providing a supportive environment. The convenient parking lot allows for easy access, and the courthouse offers a great view of the surrounding area. Visitors who have benefited from the courthouse's assistance often recommend it to others seeking help with their legal matters.

How to file a small claim case?

Chatsworth Courthouse's small claim division handles all cases in which a claim is up to $10000 for individuals and $5000 for companies. You can file a small claim case by filling out the form and submitting it at the clerk's office. Fill in your and the defendant's personal information, and tell the reason for claiming with the number of claims. You can sue a person or company if it is in Los Angeles County. You had to give $75 at the time of filing the form and the fee for serving a lawsuit is $125. After the form and documents are submitted then the court will send a trial date notice to the defendant. If the plaintiff fails to appear in court, then the case will be dismissed. After you file the case, start preparation for the trial and research the law, consult an attorney for the information, prepare the evidence, and print all the copies of the evidence for submission. The Clerk's Office at the Chatsworth Courthouse provides efficient and responsive assistance to visitors and clients.

The family law handles which types of services?

Chatsworth Courthouse family law division handles family matters that include divorce, separation, domestic violence issues, child custody, support and visitation matters. The court provides free family facilitators and self-help services to those people that cannot afford an attorney. The facilitators will guide you through the procedure but cannot provide legal advice. Many programs are provided in case of child custody matters. The Clerk's Office at the Chatsworth Courthouse is available to assist visitors with their legal inquiries and administrative needs. The Chatsworth Courthouse handles cases within the County Superior Court jurisdiction.

How can I resolve my traffic tickets?

Chatsworth Courthouse traffic division handles all traffic and vehicle violation matters. The violation includes accidents, speeding, using a mobile phone during driving, violating traffic signals and traffic rules and many more. You can receive a citation after some days of getting the traffic ticket. If the ticket contains a mandatory appearance, then you have to appear on the schedule. If the court does not contain mandatory appearance, then many options are available that are:

  • Pay the full fine on the time
  • Submit the proof of insurance
  • Contact the traffic call center and speak with the clerk about the procedure for resolving the ticket
  • Enter and send a plea to the court
  • Request for a hearing and appear before the judge
  • Request for a trial by declaration
  • Request for the removal of the license holder if your driver’s license is suspended due to an unpaid fine
  • Request for a traffic school

How many pleas can be sent to the court?

Chatsworth Courthouse plea options are available for some traffic tickets, parking and non-traffic cases. The Clerk's Office at the Chatsworth Courthouse is available to assist visitors with their legal inquiries and provide necessary administrative support. Two types of pleas are available which are:

Plea of guilty

If you are guilty of your actions then write this plea. After sending it the court will review your plea and send you the amount of the fine and there is no need to appear in court.

Plea of not guilty

If you are not guilty of your act, then write this plea. The court will give you a schedule and you have to appear on that day with your proof of innocence.

How many types of juvenile cases are handled by this court?

Chatsworth Courthouse Juvenile court handles the matters in which a juvenile is involved. Two types of juvenile cases are handled by this court that are:

Juvenile Dependency

It involves cases in which a juvenile is neglected, abused, or in danger and the guardian does not take care of them. This court was concerned with the protection of the child. The Clerk's Office at the County Superior Court provides essential administrative support and maintains accurate records of court proceedings.

Juvenile Delinquency

It involves matters in which the juvenile committed an offense that would be considered criminal if it is done by an adult.

FAQ:

Will this court provide interpreter service?

Yes, the court can provide interpreter services, you must give a request when you fill the case.

What happens if I do not pay a traffic fine on time?

If you do not pay traffic fines on time then your license will be suspended, extra fines will be added to the previous one and in serious cases, warrants will be issued against you.
